title: Monthly warmth gave no repeated gain in time-transfer predictions of fixed-size moth richness in Britain in 1992-2015
abstract: We tested whether adding monthly warmth improved moth richness predictions in another period. We fit separate English and Scottish models in 1992-2003 and 2004-2015, then predicted the other period. We controlled trap by calendar month, rainfall, sample count, sampling date and linear time. At a fixed catch size of 100 individuals, adding warmth raised mean squared error by 0.62-16.80 percent in all four main tests. Three intervals adjusted for eight tests included zero. Removing the time trend changed the small negative Scottish backward result to a gain. Raw richness gains changed sign with transfer direction in both countries. The evidence does not show a repeated prediction gain for fixed-size richness. This result does not establish no biological warmth effect. Selected months, few Scottish sites, coarse weather, uncertain trends and conditional intervals limit inference. This follow-up uses observations from a prior campaign publication. Code, source hashes, annual model losses, checks and a figure support reproduction. External record-level data remain outside the package.

display.caption: Error reduction after monthly temperature was added. Positive values mean lower mean squared error. Intervals adjust for eight main comparisons and condition on fitted training models.

citations.reason: Adapt panel construction and test temporal transfer of warmth terms. Biological records overlap. Raw sources were read again and numeric panel agreement was checked.
